verdict.line: You win if you use Q's longer range to force trades before level 6 and close the game off that lead; you lose if it drags into mid-game skirmishes where Gangplank's kit starts outscaling your single-target dive.

brief.thesis: Kled's Q (Bear Trap on a Rope, 800 range) outranges Gangplank's Parrrley (625 range), so Kled decides when fights start — which is exactly why the data shows Kled holding both the lane and solo-kill advantage here. But the head-to-head win rate is only 44.8% over 163 games, meaning that early structural edge isn't converting into games won. The gap is Skaarl's health bar: once it's chipped down by repeated poke and poison stacking, dismounted Kled deals far less damage to champions, and that's the version of Kled that shows up in Gangplank's favor later.

theirWindow.when: Gangplank Parrrleys repeatedly without trading back
theirWindow.what: He's chipping Skaarl's bar from a range you can't normally punish on reaction. Close that gap yourself — step up and land Q before he's settled into his own poke range, so the fight happens on your 800-range terms instead of his 625.

yourWindow.when: immediately after a Q hook lands
yourWindow.what: The yank guarantees the follow-up. Chain E (Joust) through him for the dash damage and speed, then pop W (Violent Tendencies) for the four empowered attacks — all three land before his Remove Scurvy can do anything but cleanse the initial shackle.

start.why: Measured at 54.8% win rate over 31 games, ahead of Doran's Blade's 45.9% — the extra sustain matters directly against Grog-Soaked Blade's stacking poison, which otherwise wins damage races it has no business winning.

boots.why: 86.8% pick rate at 45.7% win rate; flat damage reduction cuts into both his auto-attacks and the poison ticks stacking off them.

core.why: Builds the HP you need to survive the poison race while adding wave-clearing cleave damage to every trade.
Armor shred compounds with the Q-E-W burst window so each chained all-in hits harder than the last.
Part of the highest-performing listed path (66.7% win rate over 12 games); the shield covers you through Gangplank's Parrrley poke while you close distance.

situational.when: you're ahead and want to pressure towers and side lanes off your early kill lead
the poison damage race is getting close and you need more raw tankiness
you want faster joust resets for repeated all-ins in extended skirmishes
the enemy team stacks hard crowd control beyond just this lane

runes.keystoneWhy: Stacks through the sustained Q-E-W trade pattern and converts to healing, which is what actually lets you win a prolonged poison race instead of just the opening burst.

summoners.why: The dominant pick at 80.3% and the highest measured win rate (47.7%); Ignite's grievous wounds directly undercuts the heal off Remove Scurvy, turning your solo-kill advantage into finished kills instead of resets.

playing.title: Hook before he's in range
playing.detail: Kled's Q (800 range) outranges Gangplank's Parrrley (625 range). Step up and throw the bear trap first instead of walking into his poke — that's how you force the trade onto your terms.

playing.title: Chain Q into E then W
playing.detail: Land the hook-yank, immediately Joust through him for the dash damage and speed burst, then burn Violent Tendencies for the four empowered attacks. This sequence outpaces anything his poison stacking can do back.

playing.title: Protect Skaarl's bar
playing.detail: Once Skaarl's health hits zero, Kled dismounts, deals significantly less damage to champions, and loses Q for the much shorter Pocket Pistol. Don't trade into stacked poison when Skaarl is already low — disengage and let courage rebuild instead.

playing.title: Track Remove Scurvy's cooldown
playing.detail: His W clears CC and heals on an 18-22s cooldown. If you've seen him burn it recently, your next shackle-and-yank sticks for its full duration instead of getting cleansed.

playing.title: Respect level-6 Cannon Barrage
playing.detail: Once Gangplank hits 6, his R can punish an extended trade or a joust-back into open ground from anywhere on the map. Don't return-dash into space he can still hit.

playing.title: All-in during Violent Tendencies
playing.detail: W's four-attack window plus a rank-5 nine-second E cooldown means you can re-engage multiple times in one skirmish. Chain jousts instead of taking one hit-and-run.

playing.title: Don't chase past Raise Morale
playing.detail: His E buffs his and nearby allies' attack damage and movement speed for a short window. If he pops it to disengage, don't commit further than your own E's return-dash range.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, boots, runes, summoners, and all win-rate figures are measured from real games on the current patch (16.20.1) via OP.GG; the mechanical reasoning, timing windows, and trade sequencing are my own tactical reading of the ability kit, not measured data.

stats.opponentTip: Try to avoid being hit with Gangplank’s Grasp of the Undying – Parrrley (Q) combo. Be careful of his Powder Keg (E) when fighting him by using Jousting [E] to position yourself.
